Two confirmed-stale sweep targets (context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md, context/standards/shared-worktree-discipline.md) sat outside the task's creation-time file_scope in specs/state.json. Resolved at plan time by declaring both in a phase's Files to modify block, which plan-file-scope-harvest.sh harvests and plan postflight forwards to update-task-status.sh --file-scope-add; verified the harvest emits all 8 paths including the whole-tree sentinel.

Phase 2's new rules/git-workflow.md Branch section (722 B) pushed eager-load total to 71,911 B, 311 B over the Gate 20 orchestrator-context-budget.json baseline (71,600 B), causing the first deploy-headless.sh redeploy at Phase 4 to land-but-fail-verify. Two compaction passes on the new section recovered 152 B (722 -> 570 B rendered; measured eager total 71,760 B), then a reviewed, dated baseline move (71,760 B rounded up to next 100 B = 71,800 B) per the budget file's own established convention closed the remaining 160 B, matching this file's many prior precedent entries for necessary non-duplicative new rule content.

Task 675's postflight completion write was refused by the completion-deploy gate (exit 6): the deployed .claude/ tree was stale relative to the source store at completion time. Deferred to the next cycle's Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint to deploy and reconcile.

All three batched tasks declared the reserved __WHOLE_TREE__ file_scope sentinel (each owns a redeploy phase), so the in-batch admission gate deferred two of three on every cycle and the batch executed strictly sequentially. Batching bought ordering safety but zero throughput: six cycles for three tasks, with 675 deferred in cycles 1 and 685 deferred in cycles 1-4. The sentinel is too coarse to discriminate - any task carrying a redeploy phase collides with every other such task regardless of whether their real edit footprints intersect.

Identical to the 486 occurrence in the same run, and worse because this dispatch had already run deploy-headless.sh itself as its own Phase 4 (landing clean, 41 checks, 0 failures) - yet postflight still refused the completion write with exit 6 on a stale-core verdict, forcing a sixth cycle to redeploy again and reconcile. An agent-performed redeploy inside the dispatch does not clear the staleness signal the postflight gate reads, so the redeploy is effectively performed twice. Two of the run's six cycles were spent on this class alone.

Move 4's batch gate stage has now run for 30+ minutes at the close of the invocation, longer than any single implement dispatch in the run except 675's own. Gate selection picked nine suites including test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh and test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, which build throwaway fixture repos under /tmp and run the orchestrator machinery - including nested verify-deploy.sh invocations - inside them, so the gate recursively exercises the system it is gating. The stage is advisory only (it attributes findings back to tasks; it never blocks completion), and both completed tasks had already passed their own scoped verify-touched.sh runs (486: 32/32, 675: 113/113), so the marginal information is small relative to the wall-clock cost. Worth considering whether the close-of-run gate should skip suites already covered by a task's own scoped verification, or run detached from the invocation's critical path.

Repo-wide corroboration for the __WHOLE_TREE__ coarseness recorded earlier in this run: the conclusion-stage roadmap scan emitted 403 findings across 39 batches, of which 110 are __WHOLE_TREE__ file_scope collisions between a batch member and an excluded task. The sentinel is therefore not merely a local nuisance that serialized this three-task batch -- it is the dominant single cause of unformable batches across the whole backlog, because every task carrying a redeploy phase declares it and thereby collides with every other such task regardless of real edit-footprint intersection. This raises the priority of the fix from a throughput annoyance to a structural blocker on batch formation.
